predicate_sql: TRY_CAST(fair_value AS DOUBLE) = TRY_CAST(cost AS DOUBLE) AND TRY_CAST(fair_value AS DOUBLE) = TRY_CAST(principal_amount AS DOUBLE)

evidence.quote: For 2025-06-30, validated investments_at_fair_value anchor is 1608953000 and extracted holdings FV is 1975499000, residual 366546000. Rows where fair_value = cost = principal_amount contribute 96 rows and 353991000 FV, moving residual to 12555000 (0.704% of anchor).

The same exact-par predicate reduces later current-period overshoots without pushing below anchor: 2025-09-30 removes 117 rows / 394535000 FV, residual 462453000 -> 67918000; 2025-12-31 removes 133 rows / 499528000 FV, residual 549024000 -> 49496000.

The overage tracks disclosed unfunded commitments: 2025-06-30 residual 366546000 vs unfunded_commitments 339770000; 2025-09-30 residual 462453000 vs 455134000; 2025-12-31 residual 549024000 vs 548706000.

rationale: The extracted holdings include a systematic population of loan rows carried at exact par where fair_value, cost, and principal_amount are identical. In the affected 2025-H2 periods these rows explain the fair-value excess against the validated investments-at-fair-value anchor and align with the off-balance-sheet unfunded commitment signal, so they are commitment-style leakage rather than measured investment fair value. The scope excludes 2025-03-31 and earlier because applying the same predicate historically would create a new undershoot, indicating the defect is not stable there.
